Private Collector Sells 1958 Chevrolet Impala That Still Wears the Original Paint, Rebuilt V8
7 photos
Photo: eBay seller Consignify1
1958 was the year for the Impala, and this specimen is here to remind the world why. The car, which is being sold by a private collector who listed it on eBay, has already received essential work, including a rebuilt engine. It’s not a spotless Impala, so whoever buys it needs to continue the work to achieve the spotless full-size Chevy so many people are dreaming about.
The car still wears the original paint, and this is fantastic news for someone who loves the classic 1958 Impala design.
It doesn’t have the best 1958 engine, but the unit under the hood has already been rebuilt, so if you want to hop in and drive, you should be able to do that without spending more dollars.
Photo: eBay seller Consignify1 The 1957 Bel Air paved the road for an obvious Chevrolet comeback in the American car space. With the Impala presented in 1956 as a concept at GM’s motor show, it was only a matter of time until the American carmaker graduated it from the drawing board to the assembly lines.
It turns out that two years were enough, as the Impala saw daylight as a production-ready model in 1958. It wasn’t a stand-alone series but a Bel Air version - the top version, to be more precise - and it could be ordered as a hardtop and a convertible.
The Impala was the model that propelled Chevrolet to the leading spot in the United States, helping the carmaker reach sales of 1.25 million cars. Ford was the runner-up with 1.03 million cars.
The Impala wasn’t necessarily an affordable car, but it still sold like hotcakes. The hardtop started at $2,586, while the convertible carried a base price of $2,724.
Photo: eBay seller Consignify1 In addition to the Impala, the big news in 1958 was the introduction of the 348 big-block unit. This engine marked Chevrolet’s foray into the big-block world, joining the lineup with multiple configurations. The top was the M-coded Special Turbo-Thrust with an 11:1 compression ratio and solid lifters. It was an expensive engine, but it developed 315 horsepower.
It was highly desirable that year, and it is still highly desirable today. In terms of small-block power, the top configuration was the Rochester mechanical fuel-injected 283, which produced 290 horsepower but cost $484.
This 1958 Chevrolet Impala has a 283 under the hood. It has already been rebuilt, and the seller claims only 2,000 miles have been added since the work on the engine was finalized.
There are lots of new parts on this Impala, including a new clutch, a carburetor kit, new hoses and belts, a new radiator, a new fuel tank, and so on. The engine is paired with the 3-speed transmission, also original.
The mechanical part of the car is in perfect shape, so you should be able to drive it without spending a single cent.
The interior was restored to the original settings, but I would still inspect it in person to figure out how original it continues to be - and, to be honest, to determine if the work was indeed a professional restoration.
Photo: eBay seller Consignify1 The interior was replaced with original materials, according to the seller, and the objective was to redo the upholstery to the original specifications.
The Impala continues to be approximately 95% original, according to the seller.
It still wears the original paint and has power steering, power brakes, and electric wipers. It checks many boxes for a collectible, and the only part that requires some attention is the metal. There’s surface rust on the underside, so raise the vehicle on a lift if you are interested in the car, because this is the only way to determine what kind of repairs it needs.
If the damage is only on the surface, dealing with these problems shouldn’t cause any particular challenges, especially if you have a good mechanic.
Photo: eBay seller Consignify1 I don’t think this is a huge surprise, but this Impala isn’t affordable by any means. Sure, it’s not super-expensive either, and the lack of a 348 combined with that 5% that is no longer original on the car means it must be cheaper than many other siblings out there.
The seller believes $49,000 is a fair price, but if you fire up the eBay listing, you’ll discover that the Make Offer option has also been enabled. This means that you might be able to get a better deal if you are committed to a purchase, but the best way to discuss such details is during a live verification.
You can find the car parked in Canon City, Colorado, and if you live in the same state, driving the car home on its wheels could be a fantastic way to avoid the shipping costs and enjoy the time you spend behind the wheel of a 95% original Chevrolet classic. A clean title is also available, but there’s no mention of any other paperwork.
Via // eBay
